name: Dragoncult Sickle

perks.name: Hungry Edge
perks.desc: Increased sword ammo.

perks.name: Enduring Blade
perks.desc: Greatly increased sword ammo at the cost of damage.

perks.name: Honed Edge
perks.desc: Increased sword damage.

perks.name: Jagged Edge
perks.desc: Increased damage at the cost of sword ammo.

perks.name: Tempered Edge
perks.desc: Increased sword damage and ammo.

perks.name: Balanced Guard
perks.desc: Sword Guard has balanced overall defenses.

perks.name: Burst Guard
perks.desc: Sword Guard has high resistance, but low endurance.

perks.name: Enduring Guard
perks.desc: Sword Guard has high endurance, but low resistance.

perks.name: Heavy Guard
perks.desc: Sword Guard has high overall defenses, but lowers charge rate.

perks.name: Swordmaster's Guard
perks.desc: Sword Guard has low overall defenses, but increases charge rate.

perks.name: Slice
perks.desc: Casting your class ability allows this weapon to sever targets on hit for a brief duration, up to a maximum number of targets.

perks.name: Demolitionist
perks.desc: Kills with this weapon generate grenade energy. Activating your grenade ability reloads this weapon from reserves.

perks.name: Impromptu Ammunition
perks.desc: Final blows increase ammo meter progress from all sources for a short time.

perks.name: Hatchling
perks.desc: Precision final blows or rapidly defeating targets with this weapon spawns a Threadling at the target's location.

perks.name: Tireless Blade
perks.desc: Sword ammo granted for every other powered sword kill.

perks.name: Eager Edge
perks.desc: Gain increased Sword lunge distance immediately after switching to this weapon.

perks.name: Duelist's Trance
perks.desc: Sword final blows grant increased charge rate and defense until this weapon is stowed.

perks.name: Unrelenting
perks.desc: Rapidly defeating targets triggers health regeneration. Guardians and powerful combatants count as more than one kill.

perks.name: Assassin's Blade
perks.desc: Sword final blows boost movement speed and damage.

perks.name: Sword Logic
perks.desc: Final blows with this weapon grant bonus damage. The strength and duration of the bonus increases when more powerful targets are defeated.

perks.name: Attrition Orbs
perks.desc: Dealing sustained damage creates an Orb of Power.

perks.name: Chain Reaction
perks.desc: Each final blow with this weapon creates an elemental damage explosion.

perks.name: Whirlwind Blade
perks.desc: Rapid sword strikes increase this weapon's damage for a short duration. Guarding also ends the effect.

perks.name: Elemental Honing
perks.desc: Dealing unique elemental damage grants this weapon a stacking damage bonus. This bonus is increased for kinetic weapons.

perks.name: Surrounded
perks.desc: This weapon gains bonus damage when three or more enemies are in close proximity.

perks.name: Hatchling
perks.desc: Precision final blows or rapidly defeating targets with this weapon spawns a Threadling at the target's location.

perks.name: Golden Tricorn
perks.desc: Final blows with this weapon grant bonus damage. While this buff is active, grenade or melee kills of the same damage type greatly increase its damage and duration.

perks.name: Sundering
perks.desc:
Destroying vehicles and constructs or breaking target shields grants this weapon bonus reload speed and charge rate.

Constructs include barricades, turrets, Stasis crystals, and other objects created in the field.

notes: pandapaxxy (PvE / M+KB / Controller): "Dragoncult Sickle is our last dungeon weapon. Being a strand caster frame might actually benefit the toolkit a bit more. Being able to spread Sever through Slice and Chain Reaction or spawn Threadlings from a distance makes this weapon an incredibly strong addition to an all Strand loadout. It might not be the best for boss damage or the best for add clear, but I think it will find a nice home in some Strand loadouts." Recommended MW: Impact.

pandapaxxy (PvP / M+KB / Controller): "Dragoncult Sickle might have some utility in PvE but PvP is not as forgiving. Assassin’s Blade allows you to run a bit faster when you get a kill, and chain reaction will allow you to get some cheeky double kills or team wipes. I like the idea of caster frames in PvP but in practice you’re better of using another sword." Recommended MW: Impact.

Inspired by @PodvsEnemies Podcast vs Enemies episode 90 (https://open.spotify.com/episode/7C3Wx7xXVw10WshiLn5sT8?si=ZNEiHi_ZRfW5z3BbkOMrVQ) with @CourtProjects, @ImpetusAlways, and @Saint_Kabr. First-choice PvE pick for Major and Boss Spec enemies particularly for Strand subclasses in end-game content. This is the first new Caster-Frame sword we've seen in some time, and the first Strand one. Dungeon weapons tend to have better stats than world drops, and Dragoncult Sickle is no exception, having pretty good overall stats - both Impact and Ammo Capacity are higher than its peers. The advantage you have with caster frames is that you can hit from range with the heavy attack, but the ammo cost as at v7.3.0.3 is still a little high. On the other hand, you can use it for major or boss damage - the standard Jagged Edge for the extra damage and Swordmaster's Guard for the Blade and Guard perks still apply. The new-to-Season-23 Slice as the first trait perk gives this an ability to sever a major or a boss, reducing its outgoing damage by 40% for 10s (or 15s with Thread of Continuity), which can be a lifesaver in a CQC fight. In the second trait column as the signature perk, you could go for Surrounded, if you know there will be adds around to boost damage by 40%, or Whirlwind Blade if there aren't. The origin trait is situationally useful if you're in a construct-heavy environment, like the Warlord's Ruin dungeon itself. Recommended MW: Impact, with a damage boosting (Major, Boss or Taken Spec) mod.

First-choice PvE pick for add-clear of Minor Spec enemies in end-game content. This is the first new Caster-Frame sword we've seen in some time, and the first Strand one. Dungeon weapons tend to have better stats than world drops, and Dragoncult Sickle is no exception, having pretty good overall stats - both Impact and Ammo Capacity are higher than its peers. The advantage you have with caster frames is that you can hit from range with the heavy attack, but the ammo cost as at v7.3.0.3 is still a little high. If you're using this for add-clearing, one hit will equal one kill consistently so you might as well go for increased ammo with the blade perk. The origin trait is situationally useful if you're in a construct-heavy environment, like the Warlord's Ruin dungeon itself. Recommended MW: Impact, with a damage boosting (Major, Boss or Taken Spec) mod.
